data.title: Co-trimoxazole (trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole)
data.summary: Other antibacterials · Fixed combination of a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor (trimethoprim) and a sulfonamide (sulfamethoxazole) in 1:5 ratio
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antibacterials_

**Class:** Fixed combination of a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor (trimethoprim) and a sulfonamide (sulfamethoxazole) in 1:5 ratio

## Mechanism of action
- Sequential blockade of bacterial folate synthesis: sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase
- Together they are bactericidal and slow resistance

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Community MRSA skin infections (abscess, furunculosis — after drainage)
- Actinomycetoma (Nocardia): with dapsone or amikacin (two-step and Welsh regimens) — long courses
- Nocardiosis, M. marinum (limited disease), donovanosis (alternative), chancroid (older regimen)
- Pneumocystis pneumonia prophylaxis: HIV (CD4 under 200) and patients on high-dose steroids, rituximab, cyclophosphamide
- Toxoplasmosis prophylaxis, UTI, Whipple disease

## Dose & formulations
- Double-strength tablet (160/800 mg) twice daily for skin infections
- Actinomycetoma: 160/800 mg twice daily (or 8–10 mg/kg/day trimethoprim component) for many months
- PCP prophylaxis: one double-strength tablet daily or three times weekly

## Adverse effects
- Skin reactions are frequent: morbilliform rash, fixed drug eruption (a classic cause), SJS/TEN (sulfonamides are among the highest-risk drugs; much higher in HIV), DRESS, photosensitivity
- Bone marrow suppression (folate antagonism), megaloblastic anaemia; haemolysis in G6PD deficiency
- Hyperkalaemia (trimethoprim blocks ENaC), raised creatinine; hepatitis; aseptic meningitis
- Kernicterus in newborns (sulfonamide displaces bilirubin)

## Contraindications
- Sulfonamide allergy; severe liver/kidney disease; megaloblastic anaemia
- Late pregnancy and neonates under 6 weeks; G6PD deficiency (caution)

## Drug interactions
- Methotrexate: severe, sometimes fatal pancytopenia — avoid
- Warfarin (INR rises), phenytoin, sulfonylureas (hypoglycaemia)
- ACE inhibitors, spironolactone: hyperkalaemia; dapsone: more methaemoglobinaemia

## Monitoring
- CBC and potassium on long courses (mycetoma); stop at first sign of rash with mucosal involvement

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid in first trimester (folate antagonist) and near term (kernicterus) unless essential (e.g. PCP prophylaxis in HIV).

## Viva points
- Sequential block of folate pathway
- Never combine with methotrexate
- Common cause of FDE and SJS/TEN, especially in HIV
- Drug of choice backbone for actinomycetoma

_Sources: Khopkar ch.1 (Cotrimoxazole, Sulfonamides); Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
